[OC] I built F1 Almanac - An interactive archive of teammate H2Hs, driver connection webs, race visualiser and more

Hey r/formula1,

I want to share a passion project I’ve been working on: [F1 Almanac](https://f1almanac.com). 

Like many of you, I spend way too much time debating driver matchups and hunting down data to back up my takes. I built F1 Almanac to be an all-in-one interactive hub that replaces the endless tab-shuffling between Wikipedia tables, fragmented timing sheets, and scattered databases.

Here is what you can explore:

* **Teammate H2H (Qualifying & Race)**: Pick any team and season to see the complete breakdown of raw time deltas, percentage pace gaps, finishing distributions, and sprint comparisons between any two teammates. See more info [here](https://old.reddit.com/r/formula1/comments/1omcv1n/i_made_a_website_to_compare_quali_and_race_h2h/).
* **Driver vs. Driver Comparisons (Qualifying & Race)**: Compare any two drivers from a season, even if they drove for different teams.
* **Post-Race Debriefs**: Deep dive into recent Grands Prix with tyre strategy stints, degradation curves, and lap-by-lap pace progression.
* **Driver & Team Profiles**: Complete historical career timelines, stats and records of your favourite drivers and teams. 
* **Season Stats & Standings**: Historical season progression charts and results matrices.
* **Interactive Teammate Web**: The ultimate "Six Degrees of Kevin Bacon" for F1. Explore driver connections and teammate history across the entire history of Formula 1. See more info [here](https://old.reddit.com/r/formula1/comments/1uax2o1/i_built_an_interactive_f1_teammate_network_graph/).
* **2D Race Visualiser**: Relive races through an interactive replay scrubber showing relative track positions and intervals throughout the race (available for races from 2023 onwards, with Circle of Doom views back to 1996). Link [here](https://f1almanac.com/r/vis).
* **Alternative History Sandbox**: For testing every classic "what-if" debate without doing manual spreadsheet math. Reimagine any season by editing race results, dropping worst rounds, or swapping scoring rules (e.g. what if Hamilton didn't DNF in Malaysia 2016, how 2021 would look with the 1990s 10-6-4-3-2-1 system, or create your own custom point schemes) with instant points recalculations and shareable links.

Check it out here: [https://f1almanac.com](https://f1almanac.com)

I'd love to hear your feedback, bugs you spot, or any features you'd like to see next!

The degradation number teams will obsess over

Pirelli measured Friday degradation at roughly **+0.20 to +0.30 sec per lap** under the Friday conditions. At **0.30 sec/lap**, a tire could theoretically be around **4.2 seconds slower by lap 15** than at the start of the stint, ignoring fuel burn and other effects. Pirelli said the degradation was high enough that **two or potentially more stops could be competitive** which is exactly what the C2/C3/C4 allocation was designed to encourage.

text:
Some Reasons why Mercedes wasn't able to utilise Upgrade in Sepang . How Top 4 team Chassis gives them Advantage in different Tracks

It seems adding downforce to the car made their car less mechanical compliant than redbull and ferrari. As you need stiff suspension to add downforce just like mclaren and ferrari did and reaped the benefits in hungary, zandvoort, madrid , spain etc . Or you need ftm wing to produce downforce with slightly less drag.

1. ferrari have made versatile car with good front bite as well as stable rear due to high downforce. The only negative is they deforms front tyres(specially soft compound) due to front end bite with high downforce.
2. redbull have high mechanical compliance with good front end bite as seen from kerbs and bumps in monaco, austria ,baku, sepang but they lacks downforce to rivals.
3. Their pre baku floor stalled when their car was aerodynamically loaded in lateral load corners of hungary, zandvoort,madrid,spain, japan, silverstone. so they lost chunk of downforce and had snap oversteer at exit which slid their rear tyres causing overheating and degradation. it was the issue especially on low fuel or harder compound of tyres.
4. mercedes had similar mechanical compliance to redbull as seen in monaco,baku, austria, monza, sepang etc. but they lacked downforce to mclaren and ferrari which means they lost wins in spain, hungary, zandvoort, barely silverstone, and almost lost in miami, japan, madrid(vsc). In adding downforce they made their suspension stiffer which lost their mechanical compliance and produced more drag.
5. Mclaren are faster to climb the speed due to shorter gear ratio but it gets stagnated so they dont reach top speed like mercedes/alpine/williams does. Mclaren run stiff suspension to get that downforce , which destroys them in low speed corners or hard braking zones like monaco, austria, baku etc. But that downforce helped them in lateral load corners of hungary, zandvoort, madrid, japan, miami etc and even spain. Silverstone and Spa have higher speed needed , but that short gear ratio stagnated their speed, so they really struggled there.
6. See the ghost lap, how mclaren and ferrari are able to hit maximum apex speed while mercedes isnt able to, and redbull is even inferior.
7. Top4 teams: Mclaren have highest drag due to high downforce from their suspension, ferrari have 2nd highest drag, mercedes 3rd, redbull have lowest drag and lowest downforce of top4 team.
8. Fans claiming that only engine is difference from ferrari winning from mclaren, mercedes and redbull dont understand that different chasis behaves differently. Otherwise they would have done better than mercedes and redbull in monaco.
9. Small turbo helps ferrari in starts and hampers them in straights. Big turbo of redbull hampers them in starts but gives low drag and high straightline speed. Ferrari looks way worse in straights then they should have been with their engine. It is still inferior engine but not that bad as it appears due to their chassis.
10. In sepang, mercedes drag increased after adding downforce and made them less advantageous in mechanical compliant track like sepang. Mercedes will feel better in Singapore with better downforce and stable rear.
11. Drivers who prefer stable rear have mostly dominated singapore as they are able to produce less overheating of rear tyres than oversteer/ loose rear style preferring drivers. Like vettel, lewis, alonso, perez and sainz. Only time oversteery driver george won is in 2025 , the season you cant overtake after turn 1. Lando still prefers more stable rear so he also did better here. for one lap pace oversteery drivers are good in singapore but for whole race their race pace suffers due to rear tyre overheating
